help.title: Getting started
help.subtitle: What {{name}} does, how to set it up, and where everything lives.
help.askBody: Ask about the dashboard, adding {{name}} to a server, setting it up or its commands. Every answer is one of the help articles, so nothing here is made up.
help.askPlaceholder: Start typing, like “welcome message” or “level roles”
help.askNoAnswer: No help article answers that. This can only help with {{name}}: its dashboard, adding it to a server, setting it up and its commands. Try asking in other words.
help.suggestionCount_one: {{count}} suggestion. Use the arrow keys to choose it.
help.suggestionCount_other: {{count}} suggestions. Use the arrow keys to choose one.
help.browseCommandPages: Every command has its own page in the command list
help.inviteTitle: Add the bot to your server
help.inviteBody: {{name}} has to be in a server before there is anything to configure. The servers page marks the ones you can add it to.
help.pickBody: Everything you change applies to the one server you have open, and its name sits above every screen.
help.configureBody: Nothing is switched on by default. Open a section in the sidebar, turn it on, and it starts working straight away.
help.tellBody: Members use the bot in Discord rather than here. The command list says what each command does and what it takes.
help.slashDetail: Type a slash in any channel and Discord lists them, along with the options each one takes.
help.prefixDetail: The same commands, typed as ordinary text. The prefix is t? until you change it under Settings.
help.switchDetail: Any command can be turned off for one server, or for every server, without removing the bot.
help.tourSubtitle: The same list as the sidebar, with a line on each.
help.stuckBody: The support server is the quickest way to reach somebody, and the source is public if you would rather read it.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.subtitle: How this dashboard looks in your browser. Nobody else is affected.
appearance.themeDescribes: Follow the system and it changes when your device does, at sunset or on a schedule you already set.
appearance.systemHint: Match whatever this device is set to
appearance.alwaysLight: Always light, whatever the device is set to
appearance.alwaysDark: Always dark, whatever the device is set to
appearance.accentDescribes: The colour used for links, buttons and the focus ring. Green, amber and red keep their own meanings whatever you choose.
appearance.motionDescribes: Animation here is feedback rather than decoration, so turning it off costs you nothing.
appearance.motionSystemHint: Follow the reduced-motion setting on this device
appearance.motionFullHint: Animate, even where this device asks for less
appearance.motionReducedHint: Hold everything still, whatever the device asks for
appearance.languageDescribes: {{bot}}’s own messages in Discord are not translated — this is the dashboard only.

guilds.title: Servers
guilds.subtitle: Everywhere you can change {{bot}}’s settings, or add it.
guilds.emptyBody: You need Manage Server in a server before it shows up here. Ask its owner, or invite {{bot}} to one of your own.
guilds.noMatchBody: Try part of the name instead.
guilds.noPermissionHint: Adding a bot needs the Manage Server permission. Ask somebody who has it.
guilds.configurableBody: {{bot}} is in these, so every setting is one click away.
guilds.invitableBody: You have Manage Server here, so you can invite {{bot}} yourself.
guilds.lockedBody: Adding a bot takes Manage Server, which you do not have in these.

overview.subtitle: What {{bot}} is doing in this server.
overview.featuresHint: Features {{bot}} is actively running here, out of everything it offers.
overview.nothingChangedBody: Every change made from this dashboard is recorded, so you can see who turned what off and when.
overview.missingBody: These features are configured but will quietly do nothing until {{bot}} is granted them.

automod.addOneBelow: Add one below, and Discord blocks matching messages before anyone reads them.
automod.flaggedWordsAbout: Discord’s own profanity, sexual content and slur lists.
automod.keywordAbout: One word or phrase, blocked outright.
automod.limitsBody: Discord allows a handful of each kind. It refuses the rest, and this says so when it does.
automod.mentionSpamAbout: A message mentioning more people than you allow.
automod.mentionsHint: A message with more is blocked.
automod.needsManageServer: {{bot}} needs the Manage Server permission before it can read or change AutoMod rules in this server.
automod.needsPermission: Grant {{bot}} the Manage Server permission to see this server’s rules.
automod.subtitle: Discord’s own message filters. {{bot}} sets them up; Discord enforces them.
automod.title: AutoMod

auth.envBody: The dashboard is switched on but cannot sign anybody in yet. Add these to your .env and restart the bot:
auth.secretBody: Run npm run secret -- --write to generate that one.
auth.redirectBody: Then add this under OAuth2 → Redirects in the Discord Developer Portal:

auth.cancelled: You cancelled the Discord sign-in. Nothing was shared.
auth.scopes: {{name}} asks for <scope>identify</scope> to know who you are and <scope>guilds</scope> to list your servers. It never asks for your email, and it cannot read your messages through this.
auth.agree: By signing in you agree to the <terms>terms of use</terms>. What {{name}} stores is set out in the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy>.

treasure.notSetUpYet: Not set up yet — the numbers below are the defaults until you turn drops on.

treasure.dropBetween: A drop must be between {{min}} and {{max}}.
treasure.cooldownBetween: The cooldown must be between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes.

welcome.pickFirst: Pick a channel and the rest of this page turns on.
welcome.sendToHint: Everything below is stored against this channel, so it has to be chosen first.
welcome.styleCardHint: A drawn card with their avatar, plus the message.
welcome.styleEmbedHint: A coloured panel, easier to spot in a busy channel.
welcome.styleTextHint: A normal message in the channel.

welcome.title: Welcome messages
welcome.tokenCount: How many members there are now

sticky.addBody: One per channel. Editing an existing one is done above.
sticky.channelHint: {{bot}} needs permission to post here, or the sticky will never appear.
sticky.repostHint: How many messages pass before {{bot}} posts it again.
sticky.full: That is the most stickies {{bot}} can hold. Remove one to add another.

commands.switchRefused: That switch could not be saved.

levelling.subtitle: Who earns XP, what they get for it, and where it is announced.

levelling.stackHint: Off means only the highest reward role is kept as members level past each tier.
levelling.rewardsFull: That is the most rewards {{bot}} can hold. Remove one to add another.
levelling.hierarchyNote: Roles above {{bot}} in the hierarchy are hidden, because it could not grant them.

settings.title: Server settings
settings.subtitle: The switches that do not have a screen of their own.
settings.countingBody: One channel where members count upwards, one number each.
settings.countingRunHint: Off removes the configuration. The count is not kept.
settings.autoRoleBody: Given to everybody who joins, as soon as they arrive.
settings.voiceBody: Voice channels renamed to show how many members and bots the server has.
settings.prefixBody: What people type before a command name. Slash commands are unaffected by anything here.
settings.prefixAllowHint: Off means only slash commands work in this server.
settings.linkBody: Deletes links posted by anybody without the bypass permission.
settings.linkDeleteHint: {{bot}} needs Manage Messages in the channel for this to work.
settings.linkBypassHint: Anybody with this permission is never filtered.
settings.nickBody: A nickname for this server only. The picture is the same everywhere and only the bot owner can change it.
settings.nickNeedsPermission: {{bot}} needs the Change Nickname permission in this server before it can be renamed.
settings.verifyBody: A button new members press to prove they are there, and the role it hands them.
settings.verifyOnHint: Off removes the configuration. The panel already posted stops working.
settings.verifyInHint: A channel new members can see before they have the role.
settings.roleTooHigh: That role sits at or above {{bot}}’s own, so {{bot}} cannot give it to anybody. Move {{bot}}’s role higher in Server Settings → Roles, or pick a lower one.
settings.prefixSpace: The prefix cannot contain a space.
settings.prefixLong: The prefix cannot be longer than {{max}} characters.
settings.prefixSlash: A prefix starting with / collides with Discord’s own commands.
settings.countWhole: The target has to be a whole number of at least 1.
settings.countHigh: The target cannot be higher than {{max}}.
settings.cannotGiveRoles: {{bot}} cannot give {{roles}} — move its own role above them in the server settings.

owner.title: Owner console
owner.subtitle: How {{bot}} is running, and what it is being used for.
owner.membersHint: Everyone {{bot}} can see, counted across every server. People in two servers count twice.
owner.uptimeHint: Since the bot process last started, not since it last connected to Discord.
owner.mostUsedHint: Where the work goes, and where a regression would hurt most.
owner.leastUsedHint: Counted over every command the bot has, so a command nobody runs shows as zero.
owner.busiestHint: Ranked by commands run, not by how many members they have.
owner.howRunHint: Whether the prefix is still worth maintaining.
owner.screensHint: Counted bot-wide by route, with no server or account attached — see the privacy notice.
owner.nothingLoggedBody: Nothing at this level since the bot last started.
owner.nobodyBlockedBody: Anyone blocked here is refused before a command runs, in every server.
owner.nothingRunBody: Pick a command above. Its reply appears here rather than in a Discord channel.
owner.discordOnly: Part of this reply only works inside Discord. Run it there to use the controls it offered.
owner.stopping: {{bot}} is stopping. This page will stop responding in a moment.
owner.pausedBody: {{bot}} is connected but refusing everything. No commands, no XP, no automod.
owner.noCommandRun: No command has been run yet.
owner.noServerRun: No server has run a command yet.
owner.noScreenOpened: No screen has been opened yet.
owner.leaveBody: {{bot}} stops answering there immediately. Getting back in needs a fresh invite from someone still inside, and its settings are kept in case it returns.
owner.blacklistBody: A blocked account cannot run any command, on either surface, in any server. Bot-wide — to stop one command in one server, switch it off instead.
owner.idShape: A user ID is 17 to 20 digits.
owner.identityBody: The bot’s global profile, in every server at once. Discord has no per-server picture for bots — a manager gets a nickname and nothing more.
owner.renameLimit: Discord allows two username changes an hour and refuses the rest — the message below is Discord’s, not {{bot}}’s.
owner.shutDownBody: Stops the whole process, and this dashboard with it — the bot serves it. Only your host can start it again: systemd, Docker or a terminal.
owner.levelFloor: {{bot}} is running at <level>{{level}}</level>, so nothing below that is written at all. Restart it with a lower level to capture more.
owner.redactedNote: Anything that looked like a token, a password or a connection string was removed before the line was stored.
owner.runnerBody: Runs here rather than in a server: nothing is posted to Discord, and the reply comes back below. Only read-only owner commands are listed.
owner.versionBody: You are running <version>v{{version}}</version>. {{bot}} never contacts a server to check for a newer one — a self-hosted bot that phones home on a timer is not something to ship by default. Compare it against the releases page when you want to.
owner.blockListFailed: The block list could not be loaded, so this is not a list of who is blocked.

legal.englishGoverns: Translated for convenience. Where a translation and the English text disagree, the English text is the one that governs.
legal.termsSummary: {{bot}} is open-source software run by whoever set up this instance. By adding it to a server, using its commands or signing in to this dashboard, you agree to these terms.
legal.whoRunsP1: {{bot}} is self-hosted. Whoever deployed this instance — the operator — decides what it does, what it stores and who can reach it. They are responsible for it, not the project’s authors.
legal.whoRunsP2: The software is provided as-is, without warranty of any kind. Nobody promises it will be available, correct, or free of defects.
legal.whoRunsP3: The code is published under the Apache 2.0 licence with the Commons Clause. Anyone may use, change and share it, but not sell it or a paid service built mainly on it, and the credit to its original author in the NOTICE file must be kept.
legal.usingBotP1: Wherever you use {{bot}} — in a server or in a direct message — you agree to the following.
legal.usingBotL1: Follow Discord’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. They apply on top of these terms, and nothing here overrides them.
legal.usingBotL2: Do not use the bot to harass, threaten or impersonate anybody, to share illegal content, or to get round a moderation action.
legal.usingBotL3: Do not try to break, overload or take data from the bot, its database or the machine it runs on. If you find a bug, report it with /bug-report rather than using it.
legal.usingBotL4: Do not put anything into the bot — a profile, a ticket, a report, a giveaway prize — that you would not be allowed to post in Discord itself.
legal.usingBotL5: A server’s moderators, not the bot, are responsible for what happens in that server and for how its features are set up.
legal.fairUseP1: Commands have cooldowns so that one person cannot crowd out everybody else or overload the bot. The following count as abuse:
legal.fairUseL1: Sending commands, pressing buttons or triggering prefix commands far more often than using them needs — enough to disrupt a server or put load on the bot.
legal.fairUseL2: Using scripts, self-bots or several accounts to run commands, farm rewards or get round a cooldown.
legal.fairUseL3: Exploiting a bug — to duplicate coins or items, say, or to skip a cooldown — instead of reporting it.
legal.fairUseL4: Using the bot to flood a channel, mass-mention members or spam anybody.
legal.fairUseL5: Filling /bug-report, /suggest or any other free-text field with spam, abuse or anything meant to cause harm.
legal.fairUseP2: Whether something is excessive or destructive is the operator’s judgement, based on what they see in the logs and hear from the servers the bot is in.
legal.enforcement: What happens when the rules are broken
legal.enforcementP1: The operator may act without warning, in proportion to what happened:
legal.enforcementL1: Resetting coins, items, levels or anything else gained through abuse.
legal.enforcementL2: Blacklisting your account. A blacklisted account is refused every command in every server this instance serves, and is told the reason when it tries one.
legal.enforcementL3: Removing the bot from a server where it is being abused.
legal.enforcementP2: A server’s own moderators may also warn, time out or ban you there under that server’s rules. That is separate from anything the operator does.
legal.enforcementP3: If you think you were blacklisted by mistake, contact the operator of this instance. Lifting a blacklist is at their discretion.
legal.usingDashboardP1: You sign in with your Discord account. You can only configure a server where you have Manage Server, and that permission is checked live on every request, so losing it takes effect on your next click.
legal.usingDashboardP2: Every change made here is written to an audit log with your Discord account attached, so the server’s other managers can see who changed what.
legal.usingDashboardP3: Do not share your session, automate requests against the dashboard, or try to reach a server or page you have not been given. Requests are rate limited, and abusing the dashboard is treated the same as abusing commands.
legal.inBot: Economy, levels and other in-bot things
legal.inBotP1: Coins, levels, items, pets and anything else the bot tracks are virtual. They have no monetary value, cannot be exchanged for money or for anything outside the bot, and may be reset at any time by a server’s moderators or by the operator.
legal.endingP1: You can stop using {{bot}} at any time. Removing it from a server stops it acting there and deletes that server’s settings; the privacy notice says exactly what is kept.
legal.endingP2: The operator may remove the bot from a server, or block an account from using it, at their discretion.
legal.changesP1: These terms may change as the software does. The current text is always the one on this page, the project’s history is public, and using the bot after a change means accepting the new text.
legal.privacySummary: What {{bot}} collects, why, who can see it and how long it is kept. Each feature collects the minimum it needs, and nothing is sold or used for advertising.
legal.operatorP1: The operator of this instance chooses where it runs and holds its database, so they are responsible for your data here. The project’s authors never receive any of it: {{bot}} does not report back to anybody.
legal.fromDiscordP1: Like any bot, {{bot}} receives from Discord your user id, username, avatar and roles in the servers it shares with you, and the messages in channels it can see. Almost all of it is used in memory and dropped; the sections below list everything that is written down.
legal.commandsP1: Running a command, pressing one of its buttons or using a prefix command records the following:
legal.commandsL1: Command usage counts: which command, in which server, from slash or prefix, and whether it failed, per day. No user ids are stored with these.
legal.commandsL2: Cooldowns: your user id and when you last used a command, held in memory for the length of the cooldown and lost on a restart. Daily rewards and similar timers are saved with your economy record.
legal.commandsL3: Errors: when a command fails, the command, your username and user id, the server’s name and the error may be posted to the operator’s error channel so they can fix it.
legal.commandsL4: Reports: /bug-report and /suggest send what you wrote to the operator, with your username, user id and the server’s name.
legal.commandsL5: What you type into a command is used to run it and then dropped, unless saving it is the command’s purpose — a profile, a warning’s reason, a giveaway’s prize.
legal.storedP1: Each feature a server turns on keeps its own records, tied to that server:
legal.storedL1: Settings: the prefix, which features and commands are on, the channels and roles they use, and the text of welcome, sticky and ticket panel messages.
legal.storedL2: Levels: your XP, your level and when you last earned XP.
legal.storedL3: Economy: your balances, items, houses, businesses and pets, and when you last claimed each timed reward.
legal.storedL4: Moderation: warnings with their reasons and who gave them, and temporary bans until they expire.
legal.storedL5: Tickets, giveaways, lotteries and verification: who opened, joined or claimed a ticket, each giveaway’s host and winners, lottery entries and winners, and who has verified.
legal.storedL6: Counting: who counted last, so that nobody counts twice in a row.
legal.storedP2: Your profile, if you create one with /profile set, is the one record not tied to a server. It holds only what you wrote into it, anybody using the bot can view it, and /profile delete removes it.
legal.messagesP1: Messages in servers are never stored. They are read in memory for the features a server turns on — commands, automod, link filtering, counting, XP and sticky messages — and then dropped.
legal.messagesP2: If a server turns on audit logging, edits and deletions — including the earlier text of the message — are posted to a channel that server chooses. Ticket transcripts work the same way: when a ticket closes, a copy of its messages is posted to the server’s transcript channel. Both copies live in Discord, under that server’s control, not in the bot’s database.
legal.messagesP3: Direct messages are the exception. If the operator has turned on the DM log, a direct message you send the bot — its text and links to its attachments — is forwarded to the operator and kept in the database so they can reply to it.
legal.outsideP1: Nothing about you is sold or shared for advertising. A few features only work by asking another service, and send it only what they need:
legal.outsideL1: Music: what you search for or link is looked up on YouTube or SoundCloud.
legal.outsideL2: Translation, Wikipedia and Minecraft server lookups send the text, search or address you typed to Google Translate, Wikipedia or mcsrvstat.us.
legal.outsideL3: Help questions go to Anthropic when the operator has turned on AI matching, as described below.
legal.outsideL4: Commands that fetch jokes, advice, animal pictures, memes or Pokémon send only the request itself, and nothing about you.
legal.outsideP2: Each of these services handles what it receives under its own privacy policy.
legal.dashboardP1: Signing in goes through Discord’s own authorisation page. The dashboard asks for two scopes: identify, for your user id, username and avatar, and guilds, for the list of servers you are in so it can show the ones you manage. It never sees your password or email, and cannot read your messages, post as you or join servers for you.
legal.dashboardP2: Your session stores your user id, username, avatar and the tokens Discord issues, which are encrypted at rest. It ends after a few days without use — the operator chooses how many, up to 90 — and signing out deletes it straight away.
legal.dashboardP3: Every change you make is recorded with your user id and username, what changed and when, and the server’s other managers can read it. Commands the operator runs from the owner console are recorded with the options they were given.
legal.dashboardP4: Screen counts: which dashboard screen was opened, per day. They are counted bot-wide — no user id and no server id is stored with these — so they show which screens get used and nothing about who used them.
legal.dashboardP5: Requests are rate limited by session and by network address. The address is held in memory only for the length of that limit and is never written down.
legal.blacklistP1: If the operator blacklists an account, its user id and the reason given are stored so that every command refuses it. The blacklist covers every server this instance serves and lasts until the operator lifts it.
legal.logConsoleP1: The operator can read the bot’s recent log lines from the owner console. Lines can include user and server ids. Anything that looks like a token, password or connection string is removed before a line is kept, and only the last 1,000 lines are held, in memory — a restart clears them.
legal.helpQuestionsP1: A question you ask on the Help page or with /ask is matched against the bot’s help articles and then discarded. It is not stored, and it is not written to the log. If the operator has turned on AI matching, the question is also sent to Anthropic to choose an article, and nothing else about you goes with it.
legal.retentionP1: How long each kind of record lasts:
legal.retentionL1: Server settings such as the prefix, welcome, audit logging, counting and command switches: deleted when the bot is removed from that server.
legal.retentionL2: Levelling, ticket, verification, lottery and giveaway setup, and every member record — levels, balances, warnings and the rest: kept after the bot is removed, so they are still there if it is added back, until the server’s moderators reset them or the operator deletes them.
legal.retentionL3: Dashboard sessions: end after a few days without use, and signing out deletes them.
legal.retentionL4: Audit records, command usage and screen counts: 90 days, then deleted automatically.
legal.retentionL6: The DM log and the blacklist: until the operator deletes an entry.
legal.removalP1: Removing the bot from a server deletes that server’s settings, as listed above. /profile delete removes your profile at any time.
legal.removalP2: For anything else about you — your records in a server, a direct message, a blacklist entry — ask the operator of this instance. They run the database and can show it to you or delete it.
legal.ageP1: Discord requires its users to be at least 13, or older where local law says so, and {{bot}} relies on that. The only thing it keeps that touches on age is a birthday you choose to add to your profile.
legal.cookiesP1: One cookie, set when you sign in, holding a signed session identifier. It is httpOnly, same-site, and marked Secure when the dashboard is served over HTTPS. There is no third-party cookie, no advertising identifier, and nothing that follows you between sites. Your IP address is not stored, and neither is your location, your browser or your device.

status.title: Status
status.subtitle: Whether {{name}} is online, how quickly it is answering, and what it depends on.
status.headlineDegraded: Some things are slow or failing
status.unreachableBody: The dashboard could not reach the bot. It may be restarting, or the process may have stopped — only the host can start it again.
status.lastHeard: Last heard from at {{time}}. What follows is what it said then.
status.paused: Paused from the owner console, so commands are not being answered.
status.gatewayHint: How long Discord takes to acknowledge the bot’s heartbeat
status.databaseHint: How long one round trip to MongoDB takes
status.commandsHint: How long the slowest 5% of commands took in the last hour
status.historyNote: The bot records a heartbeat every five minutes. A stretch with none means it was not running, which is how an outage shows up here afterwards.
status.memoryDetail: {{used, number}} MB of a {{limit, number}} MB heap, {{rss, number}} MB in total
status.commandsIdle: None run in the last hour
status.commandsDetail_one: {{count}} run in the last hour, {{typical}} typical, {{slowest}} at the slowest; {{failures}} failed
status.commandsDetail_other: {{count}} runs in the last hour, {{typical}} typical, {{slowest}} at the slowest; {{failures}} failed
status.ytDlpMissing: Not installed, so music cannot play. Run npm run music:setup on the host.
status.ffmpegMissing: Not installed, so the volume control and tracks that are not already Opus are unavailable
status.servicesNote: Recorded from the bot’s own requests over the last hour. Nothing is contacted just to check.
status.noServices: Nothing has been called since the bot started.
